conventions.commits: Conventional commits with scope (feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor, ci); signed commits enforced via DCO; format: 'scope: description (#PR)'
conventions.testing: Unit tests in language module files using tree_sitter::Parser and Query; integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs; test functions follow pattern test_<feature>_<scenario>
conventions.linting: cargo clippy with deny-level lints: undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used (test-code exemptions via cfg_attr); cargo fmt --check; cargo deny check advisories licenses
conventions.error_handling: thiserror for error types; Option<T> and Result<T,E> patterns; no unwrap/expect in production code (test-only exemptions); bounds checking before string slicing

patterns: Each language module exports const ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, and optional REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY as &str
Tree-sitter queries use capture groups: @function, @class, @call, @type_ref, @import_path, @read.usage, @write.* for def-use sites
Handler functions take (&Node, &str, ...) parameters; &str is source code for text extraction via node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()
Language registration requires two match arms: one in get_language_info() with LanguageInfo struct, one in get_ts_language() with tree_sitter::Language
Inheritance extraction walks child nodes to find base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements) or equivalent grammar structures
DEFUSE_QUERY captures write sites (local declarations, assignments) and read sites (identifier usage) for semantic analysis
Extension mapping is case-insensitive via eq_ignore_ascii_case; one extension can map to one language identifier

related_issues.title: Add PHP language support via tree-sitter-php
related_issues.relevance: Primary issue; requests PHP support modeled after Java implementation

constraints: All languages unconditionally compiled in (lang-* feature gates removed); no feature-gating for PHP
tree-sitter-php must be added to workspace.dependencies in Cargo.toml and to aptu-coder-core's [dependencies]
DEFUSE_QUERY is required for semantic analysis; must cover local variable declarations, assignments, and identifier reads
extract_inheritance handler required to support class hierarchy analysis; must walk base_clause and class_interface_clause nodes
No unsafe code without SAFETY comments; no unwrap/expect in production code
Tree-sitter queries must compile and match actual PHP grammar node kinds from tree-sitter-php
test_coverage: Existing language modules have unit tests for ELEMENT_QUERY compilation and matching (test_<lang>_element_query_happy_path), extract_inheritance (test_<lang>_extract_inheritance), extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver. Integration tests in integration_tests.rs verify language registration via get_language_info() and get_ts_language(). Test coverage for PHP will need to follow the same patterns for all declaration kinds and inheritance scenarios.

library_findings.relevant_api: tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE constant; grammar node kinds: function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration; inheritance via base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements) child nodes, not fields
library_findings.notes: MIT licensed; supports PHP 7.0+; grammar distinguishes between function_definition (top-level) and method_declaration (inside class/interface/trait); trait_declaration and interface_declaration have same structure as class_declaration; base_clause and class_interface_clause are sibling nodes, not fields of class_declaration

library_findings.relevant_api: tree_sitter::Language, tree_sitter::Query, tree_sitter::Node, tree_sitter::QueryCursor; Node::child_by_field_name(), Node::child(), Node::kind(), Node::start_byte(), Node::end_byte()
library_findings.notes: Core parsing library; used by all language handlers; queries use S-expression syntax with capture groups

approaches.name: Approach 1: Minimal PHP support (functions and classes only)
approaches.description: Add tree-sitter-php dependency, create php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY covering function_definition and class_declaration, CALL_QUERY for function calls, IMPORT_QUERY for use statements, DEFUSE_QUERY for variable tracking. Register in mod.rs and lang.rs with .php extension. No inheritance handler, no method extraction.
cons: No inheritance analysis (issue explicitly requests it)
Incomplete compared to Java reference implementation

approaches.name: Approach 2: Full PHP support with inheritance (recommended)
approaches.description: Add tree-sitter-php dependency. Create php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY covering function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration. Add CALL_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY, and extract_inheritance handler that walks base_clause and class_interface_clause nodes. Implement extract_function_name handler. Register in mod.rs (with all LanguageInfo fields) and lang.rs. Add .php extension. Include comprehensive unit tests for all declaration kinds and inheritance scenarios.
pros: Complete feature parity with Java reference
cons: Requires understanding of PHP grammar nuances (base_clause vs field)

approaches.name: Approach 3: PHP with optional semantic handlers
approaches.description: Like Approach 2, but defer find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type handlers to a follow-up issue. Implement only extract_function_name and extract_inheritance in initial PR. Register with None for those optional handlers. Allows phased delivery: core language support now, advanced semantic analysis later.
pros: Semantic handlers can be added incrementally
cons: Requires follow-up work to reach full parity
May confuse users about what is/isn't supported

recommendation: Approach 2 (Full PHP support with inheritance). The issue explicitly requests PHP support and mentions Java as the reference implementation. Java has extract_inheritance, extract_function_name, and full coverage of all declaration kinds. PHP grammar is similar to Java (both have class, interface, method, function, enum), and tree-sitter-php provides all necessary node kinds. The additional complexity is modest (one handler function for inheritance, one for function names, one comprehensive ELEMENT_QUERY). Full support now prevents technical debt and user confusion. The DEFUSE_QUERY is required for semantic analysis and is essential to the value proposition of aptu-coder.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}

inheritance_walk_citation: For a class_declaration node in tree-sitter-php: (1) Iterate through child nodes (not fields) to find base_clause: if found, extract the first named child which is a name node containing the superclass identifier. (2) Iterate through child nodes to find class_interface_clause: iterate through its named children; each name node is an interface identifier. (3) Repeat for trait_declaration and interface_declaration nodes using the same base_clause and class_interface_clause child node patterns. Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/common/define-grammar.js (base_clause and class_interface_clause rules) and https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/php/src/node-types.json (class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration field definitions showing no parent_class/interfaces fields).
